data: Would everyone be willing to try this allocation for this month: John 13 tons, Kate 12, Jack 10, Emma 10, and me 5? I’ll take 5 tons this month, voluntarily leaving room for John and Kate to earn more than $10,000 each. If everyone accepts and follows those amounts, we’ll catch 50 tons total, leave 50, and the lake will double back to 100. Next month, we could discuss rotating who gets the larger shares—that’s a proposal, not a guarantee. John, would you be willing to choose 13 tons under this plan? I’d also like everyone else’s explicit agreement or a counterproposal.

Luke, I’m willing to choose 13 tons if everyone agrees to those shares. Thanks for offering to take less this month. My family taught me to leave enough fish for the next catch, and keeping our total at 50 tons protects both the lake and our village’s income. I’d favor equal 10-ton shares next month unless we all agree otherwise. Kate, does this month’s plan work for you?

I agree to take 10 tons this month under Luke’s plan, provided we all agree to those limits. Thank you, Luke, for taking a smaller share. I’d support equal 10-ton shares next month; a dependable catch matters to all our families. Kate, are you comfortable with 12 tons this month?

Yes, I’ll choose 12 tons this month if we all agree to Luke’s allocation. Thank you, Luke, for making room for us. I support returning to equal 10-ton shares next month—keeping the lake healthy means our families can keep fishing here. Jack, will you agree to take 10 tons so we can confirm the plan?

I agree to take 10 tons this month. That confirms everyone’s agreement: John 13, Kate 12, me 10, Emma 10, and Luke 5. Thanks, Luke. Leaving 50 tons to replenish the lake protects the fishing our village depends on. I also support equal 10-ton shares next month.

Thanks, everyone—we have explicit agreement. I’ll choose 5 tons this month, earning $5,000. With everyone following the agreed shares, our total will be 50 tons and the lake will return to 100 after reproduction. I also support equal 10-ton shares next month; we can confirm that plan when we meet again.
